plan.title: rfc(hooks): enforce on the merge path where it runs the full gate set; keep a small local hook floor

narratives.Description: Local hooks refuse many agent actions before a pull request exists; in a repository whose merge path already runs the full gate set, most of those refusals stop legitimate work and catch nothing the merge path does not. This story lets a closed set of named local refusal sites warn instead of refuse, but only when the check named by plan.policy.mergeGateContext in the project definition at the delivery-branch head on GitHub is also in the branch's live required status contexts; every other refusal, and every repository without that signal, keeps refusing as today.
narratives.Overview:
1. Merge-gate name. The project definition may carry `plan.policy.mergeGateContext`, the name of one required status check that runs the repository's full merge gate. The hook reads it only from GitHub: the project definition file at the head of the delivery branch, through the contents API, inside the bounded read of item 2. It never takes the name from the worktree copy or from a local ref. The worktree copy is a trigger only: the hook makes the GitHub read only when the worktree copy names a check, and the signal needs the GitHub copy to name the same check. Absent, empty, different or unreadable means no signal.
2. Live check. At a warn site, after item 1 yields a name, the hook calls the existing `fetchRequiredStatusContexts` for the repository and delivery branch with a gh runner whose timeout keeps the whole read (item 1 and item 2 together) well under the host hook timeout. The signal holds only when the read did not fail and its contexts include the named check. A failed read, a timeout, or a list without the name means no signal. The result is reused for the rest of that hook call and is not written anywhere.
3. Warn sites. Exactly these sites can warn: (a) the `ritual.code !== 0` arm of the gated ritual (stale, missing or other-worktree ritual state, and a failed ritual step, agent-hook readiness included); (b) the write-path `scope-not-ready` return when the worktree binding did not refuse (multiple eligible, zero eligible, env pin miss); (c) the positive governing-allow check on a selected story's `file_scope`; (d) the `prospective-scope-cover-deny` returns for staged paths outside `file_scope` and for the index-snapshot file-set check; (e) the story write fence's `deny-story-scope` verdict in runtime authority (a direct-write path outside the selected story's `file_scope`). These stay refusals: the runtime-authority refusals other than `deny-story-scope` (project `denyPaths` and `allowPaths`, `scopes.edits` false, an unreadable story fence, unclassified or unsupported targets), the ritual inspection throw, the compact-heal refusal, `occupancy-ritual-mismatch`, a binding refusal, an unresolvable commit target, an unreadable index, unreconstructable shell write dests, dest-form expansion, `spawn-not-ready`, and every other refusal code.
4. Continue, do not return. Under the signal, a warn site records its refusal text as a warning and evaluation continues. On the shell path the commit check returns no decision and passes the warning on. A later refusal wins. The final allow carries the warnings.
5. Warning output. The final allow's message starts with `Warning:` and, for each warning, gives today's refusal text and one clause that local enforcement is advisory because the named check is required on the delivery branch. It does not claim that check enforces the same condition. It uses the existing tool.before allow-advisory rendering. No new log or file.
6. Floor statement. Every refusal not listed in item 3 keeps today's behaviour, including protected stores, the kill-switch, occupancy, the intent ceiling, foreign repositories, tree-wide destructive git and default-branch push and force push. This design adds no guard for secrets paths, deletes outside the repository or force pushes to other branches.
7. No local signal state. No record, cache file, flag or table mode selects warn. The #1517 record and the #6281 table are not read or changed.
8. Docs. One section in the hooks docs names `plan.policy.mergeGateContext`, the warn sites, the floor statement, and the limits in item 6 and in "What it does not do".

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given no `mergeGateContext` in the worktree copy of the project definition, when a warn site fires, then the hook refuses as today and makes no GitHub call.
- Given a worktree copy that names a check and a GitHub copy at the delivery-branch head that names none or a different check, when a warn site fires, then the hook refuses as today and makes no required-context call.
- Given a worktree copy of the project definition that names a merge-gate check and a delivery-branch head on GitHub that does not, when a warn site fires, then the hook refuses as today.
- Given a local `origin/<deliveryBranch>` ref repointed at a commit whose project definition names an unrelated required check, and a delivery-branch head on GitHub that names none, when a warn site fires, then the hook refuses as today.
- Given a named check that is in the delivery branch's live required contexts, when a stale ritual blocks a product write, then the write is allowed and the message starts with `Warning:` and contains the ritual refusal text.
- Given a named check that is not in the live required contexts, when a warn site fires, then the hook refuses as today.
- Given a required-context read that fails or times out, when a warn site fires, then the hook refuses as today.
- Given the signal, two or more active briefs, an unbound linked worktree inside the repository folder and a product write there, then the write is allowed with a warning.
- Given the signal and a worktree binding that refuses, when a product write fires, then the hook refuses as today.
- Given the signal and a stale ritual, when the write targets a protected store, then the protected-store refusal is returned.
- Given the signal and a shell command that commits paths outside `file_scope` and also writes a protected store, then the protected-store refusal is returned.
- Given the signal and a commit of staged paths outside `file_scope`, then the commit is allowed with a warning.
- Given the signal, a selected story with a non-empty `file_scope` and a direct write outside it that no project policy refuses, then the write is allowed with a warning.
- Given the signal and a direct write that project `denyPaths` or `allowPaths` refuses, then the hook refuses as today.
- Given the signal and a ritual inspection that throws, then the hook refuses as today.
- Given the signal and `spawn-not-ready`, `installation-identity-deny`, `occupancy-occupied`, `git-destructive-deny` or `foreign-repository-deny`, then the hook refuses as today.
- Given a warned allow on each of the Grok, Cursor, Claude and Codex hosts, then the rendered output carries the warning text in that host's advisory field.
- Given any run under the signal, then no file under `.deft/` records the signal.

narratives.UserStory: As a maintainer of a repository whose merge path runs the full gate set, I want the local hook checks that duplicate that merge path to warn instead of refuse, so that workers in linked worktrees stop hitting false-positive refusals while protected stores, the kill-switch, occupancy and every other floor refusal stay fail-closed.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/gh.ts: split defaultRunGh into a runner that takes a timeout in milliseconds and add makeBudgetedRunGh(budgetMs, now), a RunGhFn that gives each call the time left of one shared budget and returns a failed result (returncode -1, no throw) once the budget is spent.
2. New packages/core/src/hooks/merge-gate-signal.ts: readMergeGateContext(projectDefinition) returns the trimmed plan.policy.mergeGateContext string or null; createMergeGateSignal({ root, runGit, runGh }) returns a lazy, per-hook-call memoized isLive(). It reads the worktree copy first (no name means false with no GitHub call), then derives the repository from `git remote get-url origin` and the delivery branch from resolveDeliveryBranch, then with ONE budgeted runner reads the project definition at the delivery-branch head through the GitHub contents API (the GitHub copy must name the same check) and calls fetchRequiredStatusContexts; it is live only when neither read failed and the contexts include the name. It never reads a local ref as authority, writes no file or record, and has no throw, reject or abort site. The read budget is one owned named constant, MERGE_GATE_SIGNAL_READ_BUDGET_SECONDS = 10 (well under the 30 s tool.before host timeout); it is a numeric-const fact, so the brief declares plan["x-directive/intentConstraint"] (10 seconds, operation) for the operator mint (value named by the operator).
3. packages/core/src/policy/runtime-authority.ts: the deny-story-scope result of evaluateRuntimeAuthorityDirectWrite carries storyScopeOnly: true; code and reason text do not change, and the project denyPaths and allowPaths verdicts are untouched.
4. packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts: add a mergeGateRunGh seam and one lazy signal plus a warnings list per inspectMutationGates call. Sites that warn instead of return when the signal is live: (a) the ritual.code !== 0 arm after the compact-heal check; (b) the non-spawn scope-not-ready return when the worktree binding did not refuse and denyKind is multiple-eligible, zero-eligible or pin-miss; (c) requirePositiveGoverningAllow on a non-spawn write and in the commit cover; (d) the commit path's staged-paths-outside-file_scope result (new kind on ProspectiveScopeCoverResult) and the index-snapshot word result; (e) the deny-story-scope verdict in runtimeAuthorityForDirectWrite via a warning sink. Each warning is today's refusal text plus one clause that local enforcement is advisory because the named check is required on the delivery branch; every allow message built after the ritual starts with `Warning:` and then carries the warnings (withOccupancyWarning). decideProspectiveGitCommitScopeCover takes a warnings sink and returns null so the shell route continues to the write reissue and dest-forms checks, and the final shell allow carries the warnings. No other refusal changes.
5. packages/types/schemas/vbrief-core-0.6.schema.json and content/vbrief/schemas/vbrief-core.schema.json (kept in sync): document plan.policy.mergeGateContext as a string or null.
6. content/docs/hook-root-admission.md: one section naming mergeGateContext, the warn sites, the floor statement and the limits. Use no rule keywords so docs/RULE-MAP.md does not change.
7. Tests: merge-gate-signal.test.ts, dispatcher-merge-gate-warn.test.ts (all four hosts), runtime-authority.test.ts, gh.test.ts. No new numeric const, throw, reject or abort outside the one declared constant.
8. changelog.d/6535-hooks-warn-where-merge-gate-is-live.md.

### 1. blocks-the-design — `configured` is not evidence the merge path runs the scope and lifecycle checks

When a `configured` record exists and the live inventory later becomes `absent`, strategy start returns failure and does not rewrite the file (`compute.ts:1026-1036`). When the inventory is still merely non-empty, it returns the old record without refreshing `contexts` (`compute.ts:1001-1011`). Two docs in this tree disagree about this repository's required checks: `content/scm/github.md:727-731` says the merge-gate aggregator is not required, and `content/docs/github-merge-queue-setup.md:111` plus `docs/RELEASING.md:39-41` say `Merge gate (task check)` and `Greptile Review` are required. An agent, including one following a prompt to write the JSON, can create that decision in `.deft/merge-gate-enforcement/` because the directory is ordinary ignored state. The hook then warns on ritual, scope, and commit checks in a repository that has nothing behind them. After the required checks are removed, the file still says `configured`, and a reader that looks only at the decision still warns. The injection path is the same write: the signal is shared local state, and one tool call changes authority for later tool calls in every worktree of that checkout.

Disposition. The mechanism cannot bind on this signal. The form that passes does not read the on-disk decision as authority. In the same hook call it uses the existing `fetchRequiredStatusContexts` result for the delivery branch. A downgrade happens only when that result is not a failed resolution and the context labels include the checks that enforce the work being downgraded, the scope and lifecycle checks on the merge path. A non-empty list that lacks those labels stays fail-closed, which is what keeps a build-only repository on today's denials. A file cache of the read is the same forge. This read can make the hook slower. The Grok host already proceeds when the wrapper produces no decision (`packages/core/src/init-deposit/agent-hooks.ts:104-108`). That residual stays #5920, which this arc leaves deferred. The passing form does not describe a timed-out hook as a warning or as a successful signal.

## Bound remedy
1. Merge-gate name. The project definition may carry `plan.policy.mergeGateContext`, the name of one required status check that runs the repository's full merge gate. The hook reads it only from GitHub: the project definition file at the head of the delivery branch, through the contents API, inside the bounded read of item 2. It never takes the name from the worktree copy or from a local ref. The worktree copy is a trigger only: the hook makes the GitHub read only when the worktree copy names a check, and the signal needs the GitHub copy to name the same check. Absent, empty, different or unreadable means no signal.
2. Live check. At a warn site, after item 1 yields a name, the hook calls the existing `fetchRequiredStatusContexts` for the repository and delivery branch with a gh runner whose timeout keeps the whole read (item 1 and item 2 together) well under the host hook timeout. The signal holds only when the read did not fail and its contexts include the named check. A failed read, a timeout, or a list without the name means no signal. The result is reused for the rest of that hook call and is not written anywhere.
3. Warn sites. Exactly these sites can warn: (a) the `ritual.code !== 0` arm of the gated ritual (stale, missing or other-worktree ritual state, and a failed ritual step, agent-hook readiness included); (b) the write-path `scope-not-ready` return when the worktree binding did not refuse (multiple eligible, zero eligible, env pin miss); (c) the positive governing-allow check on a selected story's `file_scope`; (d) the `prospective-scope-cover-deny` returns for staged paths outside `file_scope` and for the index-snapshot file-set check; (e) the story write fence's `deny-story-scope` verdict in runtime authority (a direct-write path outside the selected story's `file_scope`). These stay refusals: the runtime-authority refusals other than `deny-story-scope` (project `denyPaths` and `allowPaths`, `scopes.edits` false, an unreadable story fence, unclassified or unsupported targets), the ritual inspection throw, the compact-heal refusal, `occupancy-ritual-mismatch`, a binding refusal, an unresolvable commit target, an unreadable index, unreconstructable shell write dests, dest-form expansion, `spawn-not-ready`, and every other refusal code.
4. Continue, do not return. Under the signal, a warn site records its refusal text as a warning and evaluation continues. On the shell path the commit check returns no decision and passes the warning on. A later refusal wins. The final allow carries the warnings.
5. Warning output. The final allow's message starts with `Warning:` and, for each warning, gives today's refusal text and one clause that local enforcement is advisory because the named check is required on the delivery branch. It does not claim that check enforces the same condition. It uses the existing tool.before allow-advisory rendering. No new log or file.

Every refusal not listed in item 3 keeps today's behaviour, including protected stores, the kill-switch, occupancy, the intent ceiling, foreign repositories, tree-wide destructive git and default-branch push and force push. ## In plain English

Problem: local hooks refused many agent actions before a pull request existed. In this repository and in a consumer report, most of those refusals stopped legitimate work and caught no real defect; the real catches came from the merge path. The local layer also fails open when a hook runs past the host timeout at large worktree counts (#5920).

Accepted solution: a few named local checks warn instead of refuse, but only where the merge gate is live, and everything else refuses as today. The project definition may name one required check as the merge gate (`plan.policy.mergeGateContext`). The worktree copy of that field is only a trigger: with no name there, nothing changes and no GitHub call is made. With a name there, at a warn site the hook reads the name from the project definition at the head of the delivery branch on GitHub and the branch's live required checks, in one read with a short timeout. Only when GitHub names the same check and lists it as required does the site warn; a failed read, a timeout or a mismatch refuses as today. The warn sites are the gated session ritual, the not-ready scope fence when no worktree binding refused, the story `file_scope` checks on writes and commits, and the commit index-snapshot check. A warn site records the warning and evaluation continues, so every later check still runs and any later refusal wins. The warning uses the existing `Warning:` channel that all four hosts render.

The design adds no gate, grant, refusal, verb, local record or protected path. Limits stated and accepted: it does not fix the hook timeout fail-open (#5920, operator-deferred); it adds no guard for secrets paths, deletes outside the repository or force pushes to other branches, none of which exists today (the secrets-path gap is a known gap for its own issue); commit verdicts for worktrees inside and outside the repository folder still differ until #6471; a wrong merge-gate name, or a repository where an agent can merge its own pull request, weakens only that repository. The #1517 record is not used as the signal.

## Proposal

Where a repository's merge path runs the full gate set (CI merge gate, merge queue, review bots, human-only mints), local hooks keep only a small hard floor and every other local check becomes warn-only. Repositories without that merge path keep today's fail-closed hooks. Bound worktrees (#6379) may then work inside the main checkout's folder as well as outside it.

Operator decisions (2026-11-17): lead with this option; no trial period, the evidence below is enough; the floor below is acceptable.

## Why

On 2026-11-16/17 this repo shipped two releases and about 15 stories with workers that ran in linked worktrees outside the repo folder, each bound to one story by `swarm:pre-dispatch` (#6379). In that setup the local multi-active write fence is skipped (#2885 / #3794). Every real defect in the period was caught on the merge path. Most local hook refusals were false positives or friction.

### What caught real defects (all on the merge path)

- `verify:class-checks` class 4: a protected authz file mixed with story files (#6187), split into its own PR.
- `verify:scope-provenance`: a spec-drift row outside the brief's membership (#6481, filed as #6508).
- CI smoke and both merge gates: a CLI crash at load from an import cycle (#6468), which unit tests missed.
- `verify:changelog-unreleased`, `verify:docs-impact`, `pr:check-closing-keywords`: missing fragment or block, caught before merge.
- Review bots: real Greptile P1s on #6187 (five bypass variants), #6422, #6480.
- Human-only steps: intent-constraint mints for new constants (#6423, #6378), release cuts.

### What local hooks refused

- Commit-text check (#5656): heredoc text that mentions a commit (#6187), a trailing `2>&1 | tail -N` (#6471), and the coordinating session's own note to a file. No real catch observed.
- Stale session ritual: workers refused until `session:start --session-id=<own id>`; the coordinating session's memory and note writes refused after 8 h. No real catch observed.
- In-PR completion locked the worktree binding (#6480): six operator-run commit scripts on one story.
- The session hook rewrote tracked `AGENTS.md` from the pinned runtime in every worktree (#6507), a regression risk if committed.
- Occupancy lease: one refusal of the coordinating session's local update while another session held the primary checkout. Real coordination, worked as intended.
- Protected stores (`.deft/authz/`, `.deft/approved-scope/`): writes stayed human-only, as intended. A worker still read `.deft/approved-scope/` through `git grep`, which the hook did not see, so the read rule is not complete anyway.
- Hook latency: at 97 linked worktrees a Grok `tool.before` hook hit its 30 s cap and failed open (#5920), so the local layer was not a reliable control at that scale.

### Consumer evidence (a consumer report, Nov 4-11)

69 denials in a week, of which the groups listed did not catch real problems; `session:ready` run 98 times; agents wrote files through scripts 21 times to get around the fence; about half of the lead agent's tool calls went to process.

## Shape

1. Hard local floor (fail-closed everywhere): writes to protected stores (grants, mints, approved scope), push to or destructive verbs on the default branch, the kill-switch, secrets paths, and the occupancy lease between concurrent sessions.
2. Warn-only where the merge path runs the full gate set: commit-text shape, stale ritual, prospective scope cover, the multi-active fence, AGENTS and deposit checks. The merge path keeps enforcing scope and lifecycle.
3. A detectable signal that a repository's merge path runs the full gate set, for example the recorded merge-gate enforcement state (#1517). Without the signal, today's fail-closed behaviour applies.
4. Bound worktrees (#6379) are admitted inside the repo folder on the same terms as outside it.

## Alternatives considered

- A. Keep today's model: all local hooks fail closed. Cost as above.
- B. The floor and warn-only for every repository. Consumers without CI merge gates would lose protection.

## Risks and open questions

- Which prompt-injected local actions that never reach a PR (deleting files, force pushes, writing secrets) must the floor cover beyond the list above?
- Warn-only output must stay visible, or agents ignore it. The #6281 warn-first design and #6139 (one next command per deny) apply.
- What exactly counts as "the full gate set", and who records it?

## Related

#5920, #5988, #6139, #6185, #6281, #6292, #6379, #6469, #6471, #6480, #6507, #1517, #3156 (gate integrity: this change goes through issue and review, never by editing a gate to go green).
